name: Dead bug and bird dog
pattern: Opposite arm and leg reach out while the trunk holds still: face up (dead bug) or on hands and knees (bird dog).
setup: Dead bug: lie on your back, arms pointing at the ceiling, hips and knees bent 90 degrees.
Bird dog: hands under shoulders, knees under hips, back flat.
Brace lightly so the low back does not move.

steps.text: Slowly reach one arm and the opposite leg away from you.
Pause for a breath with the trunk perfectly still.
Bring them back and switch sides.

cues.cue: Move the limbs, not the spine.
cues.why: These drills train the trunk to stay stiff while the limbs load it, with modest spine compression.

cues.cue: Dead bug: low back stays in contact with the floor.
cues.why: Dynamic stabilization drills aim to keep the lumbar spine still while the limbs move.

cues.cue: Bird dog: hips level, like a glass of water on your back.
cues.why: Hip rotation is the most common way to cheat the reach.

cues.cue: Reach long; don't lift the leg higher than the hip.
cues.why: Lifting higher arches the low back and raises spine load.

cues.cue: Slow: hold each reach for a breath or up to 10 s.
cues.why: Slow reaches with short holds are the standard progression for this drill.

breathing: Breathe out as you reach, in as you return; keep breathing during holds.

tempo.note: Reach in 2 s, hold 2-10 s, return in 2 s.

mistakes.name: Low back arches
mistakes.looks: Dead bug: the low back lifts off the floor as the leg lowers. Bird dog: the belly sags.
mistakes.fix: Shorten the reach or keep the knee bent.
mistakes.why: The trunk has lost control of the pelvis.

mistakes.name: Hips tip or rotate
mistakes.looks: Bird dog: the lifted-leg hip opens toward the ceiling.
mistakes.fix: Point the lifted toes at the floor; keep both hips level.
mistakes.why: Rotation lets you reach without stabilizing.

mistakes.name: Rushing
mistakes.looks: Limbs swing out and back without a pause.
mistakes.fix: Pause for a full breath at full reach.

safety: Low back pain: these are often well tolerated; start with arm-only or leg-only reaches.
Wrist or knee pain in bird dog: use a cushion under the knees and fists or forearms.

variants.change: Holding a load or pressing a ball between hands and knees raises the abdominal demand.
Different support, same rule: limbs move, trunk stays still.

harder: bird dog from a plank (bird dog plank)

subtypes.name: Bird dog
subtypes.change: On hands and knees; reach the right arm forward and left leg back.

motion.basis: Default is the dead bug (right arm and left leg reach). Starting 90/90 positions are the standard setup; reach angles estimated. Bird dog spine-load findings from callaghan1998 and kavcic2004.
